# A real PLG100-VL talking to a real S-MU2000, captured in MAME.
#
# This is the reference the answer card is built from, and it is here because the
# firmware's own "PB Com Error!" told us the stub was answering too little: the VL
# keeps 680 messages in flight over 120 s across FOUR device channels, and
# answer.c implements one of them.
#
# MAME, 40 s... no: 120 emulated seconds, warm NVRAM:
#   ./mame mu2000 -rompath ./roms/dump -plg1 plg100vl -video none -sound none \
#       -seconds_to_run 120
# Timestamps are emulated seconds. This is the byte stream, not the line: the
# card sees the same 31250 baud 8N1 the chip does.
#
#   host -> card  680 messages, 7894 bytes
#   card -> host  650 messages, 8458 bytes
#
# Channels, by the two bytes after F0 43 10:
#   4e  control. read announces and polls; the card answers a poll with the
#       address it was asked for. This is the only channel answer.c speaks.
#   4c  sixteen voice slots, 08 00 35 01 .. 08 0f 35 01, one per slot.
#   4f  polls answered with 13- and 42-byte payloads - tone and parameter blobs.
#   40 03 -> 43 40 43, 12 bytes each, 595 of them. The bulk of the traffic.
#
# The category is the second thing that differs from the AP: the VL answers
# 00 00 00 where the AP answers 00 07 00, and its name is PLG100-VL. answer.c
# presents the AP's, which is the card that does not work.
#
# --- host -> card ---
    3.8139  f0 43 10 4e 00 10 02 01 f7
    3.8167  f0 43 30 4e 01 10 00 f7
